blocks.content: This topic ties liveness, readiness, and startup probes together, covering how they are commonly combined in practice, and the tuning parameters that determine how patient or aggressive each check actually is.

Recapping the previous three topics precisely: liveness asks "should this be restarted," readiness asks "should this receive traffic right now," and startup asks "has this finished booting yet," three distinct questions, not three variations of the same check.

blocks.alt: Three distinct questions, not interchangeable variations of the same idea

blocks.content: A real production service, particularly one with a non-trivial startup sequence, often uses all three together: a startup probe to patiently wait out the initial boot, then liveness and readiness probes actively monitoring it for the rest of its running life.

blocks.alt: All three working together, each covering a different phase and concern

blocks.content: 3. Tuning How Patient or Aggressive a Probe Is
blocks.text: 3. Tuning How Patient or Aggressive a Probe Is

blocks.content: initialDelaySeconds (how long to wait before the first check at all), periodSeconds (how often to check), and failureThreshold (how many consecutive failures before acting) together tune exactly how forgiving or strict a probe actually behaves.

blocks.alt: The dials that decide exactly how forgiving or strict a given probe actually is

blocks.content: A genuine mistake worth avoiding: a liveness probe endpoint that itself performs deep, expensive checks, verifying every downstream dependency, a slow database call, and similar, a transient blip in one dependency can trigger unnecessary restarts of an otherwise perfectly healthy application.

blocks.alt: A health check that checks too much, causing unnecessary restarts from unrelated issues

blocks.content: The right approach probes exactly what each check is actually meant to verify, liveness should confirm the application process itself is genuinely responsive, nothing deeper, readiness can afford to check a bit more (like a critical dependency actually being reachable), since its failure mode is just "hold off traffic," not "restart the container."

blocks.alt: Checking exactly the right thing for each probe type, and no more than that

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Liveness, readiness, and startup probes answer three genuinely different questions, and a real production service commonly combines all three deliberately.
A liveness probe checking too much (deep downstream dependencies) is a genuine, common anti-pattern, causing unnecessary restarts from unrelated, transient issues.
